headline: Three futures for 2030: optimistic, base, downside
definition: Optimistic = the carriers' view: a tight market with little overcapacity

inputs.by: low · mid · high, from the orderbook
Drewry Issue 2; spread from past forecast errors

inputs.v: 2027 60% · 2028 20% · 2029 10% · never 10%; 0.4 to 1.5 M TEU still on the Cape

fan.label: Median gap at the peak: 5.98 M TEU of deliveries land in 2028 (Alphaliner)
fan.note: Band = P10 to P90 of 5,000 runs. Gap above zero: supply grows faster than demand.
fan.insight: Even the optimistic edge is +7.1 pp in 2028: 9 runs in 10 show more than 7 pp of overcapacity at the peak.

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.story: Demand runs about 2.3 pp a year above Drewry’s path: the gap peaks at +8.0 in 2028 and is back to about zero by 2030.
scenarios.act: Hold newbuild slots back, add no new orders, keep scrapping steady.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.story: Demand follows Drewry, about a quarter of the 2028 deliveries slip and 2.3 M TEU are scrapped: the gap peaks at +10.7 in 2028 and is +1.8 in 2030.
scenarios.act: Blank sailings and slow steaming to protect rates, scrap the oldest ships.

scenarios.name: Downside
scenarios.story: Demand runs about 2.3 pp a year below Drewry and less is scrapped: the gap peaks at +13.0 and is still +4.3 in 2030.
scenarios.act: Deeper blank sailings, scrap beyond the 0.655 M TEU record (needs yards) and consolidate.

spread: The three paths differ mostly in demand (about 2.3 pp a year either way). Suez timing, slippage and 2030 deliveries barely separate them.
signposts: Demand against Drewry’s +4.2% for 2027: the biggest swing between our three paths.
Suez share of Asia–Europe capacity (36% in early Oct 2026, Clarksons): a quick rise means Cape capacity returns early.
Hormuz reopening: BIMCO’s 2027 ship demand is 2 pp higher in its open case.
Slippage and new orders after Oct 2026, ahead of the 5.98 M TEU due in 2028.
limits: Not modelled: port congestion, slow steaming, consolidation, Hormuz after 2027, new orders after Oct 2026.
The band is probably too tight: only 5 of 10 published fleet forecasts fall inside our P10 to P90.
Ranges are our own estimates: a simulation, not a forecast. Scenarios = median of the runs around P10, P50 and P90 of the 2030 utilisation index.
